onnxruntime-web 1.30.0 - vendored, served from this origin (no CDN)
====================================================================

Source:   npm package onnxruntime-web@1.30.0 (npm pack onnxruntime-web@1.30.0)
          tarball sha512-q0y+JrrtukXSzsBWEMccVfqX25LRmosXHF+CaRJmg8pZClzcV7svNc4rKY3jL02Vb7QmRMDs1SigqR4CXAfKYQ==
          (shasum b88b09117992e6f486321e931a826fd2f7775377)
Matches:  onnxruntime==1.30.0 in ai/requirements-serve.txt (the Python serving path)
Licence:  MIT (below)
Used by:  scan.html / scan.js (the live road scan), via dynamic import()

Files copied unmodified from the package's dist/ folder:

  ort.all.min.mjs                    sha256 2e4a0eae53c3f246e26423aaca493d3bfc22ce524894f27519a9ec4a14e6397a
  ort-wasm-simd-threaded.jsep.mjs    sha256 709853412fd1ffc34247af1e73569227b5b79629c5ca3f59cc39cf7e500e4947
  ort-wasm-simd-threaded.jsep.wasm   sha256 3ad23231b5bd6d9dda55a7f84606315e0bf35b6750c28ee993c987c54cacab0f

Why these three: ort.all bundles the WebGPU, WebGL and WebAssembly execution
providers; WebGPU and WebAssembly both run on the "jsep" WebAssembly build, so
that is the only .wasm needed. scan.js sets ort.env.wasm.wasmPaths to this
folder, so the runtime never falls back to fetching its files from a CDN.

Why vendored rather than an npm dependency: the API serves apps/web as static
files with no build step, and a dependency would still need copying here. The
hashes above are what a reviewer checks an upgrade against.

To upgrade: npm pack onnxruntime-web@<version>, copy the same three files from
package/dist/, update this note and the version string in scan.js, and rerun
app/scripts/scan-check.mjs (it compares the page's detections with serve.py's).
